captions.detailed: This 3D model represents a BMX jump fork and steering assembly. It features a wide triple-clamp crown, two parallel round-section fork legs, and a central head tube in a light gray finish. A black mounting bracket projects forward from the head tube. Mounted above is a quill stem holding wide, upswept light-gray riser handlebars finished with black cylindrical hand grips. The steering assembly is designed to rotate relative to the frame mount along the central steering axis.
captions.instruction: Create a 3D model of a BMX jump fork and handlebar steering assembly. The assembly should feature a light gray triple-clamp crown, parallel cylindrical fork legs, a central head tube with a forward-extending black frame mount, and wide upswept handlebars with black hand grips. Ensure the steering assembly is articulated to rotate relative to the fixed frame mount.
captions.factory: Construct the fixed frame mount as a black component using a combination of a cylinder for the head tube sleeve and an extruded profile or box for the forward mounting arm. For the steering assembly, model the fork legs and steerer tube as cylinders, and construct the triple-clamp plates as extruded flat shapes. Create the handlebars using a swept circle along a curved wire path, adding cylindrical grips at the ends. Assemble these parts using a revolute joint representing the steering axis, allowing the fork, stem, and handlebars to rotate relative to the stationary frame mount.
